review_text_raw:
Simulacra 3 is a game that is genuinely interesting most of the time. Which is about the biggest compliment I can give it. Now the rest isn't all THAT bad, but it's certainly not on par with Sara is Missing or the original Simulacra. It's a found phone game that could've evolve to be so much more, but instead finds itself stuck with more of the same formulaic problems from previous iterations of the game. Here's some spoiler free bullet points on the game. TLDR at the bottom 

The Story. 
The story is easily the best part of the game. It's fairly interesting, if you've played the previous games, you pick up on a lot of what's going on and the game makes some references to them, but it's definitely not necessary to play the previous games. There's enough of a mystery here that it's kinda neat to unravel. 

Horror 
This is easily the weakest part of the game. I can't express how much I hate this asinine "horror" element. Since the last game, I've called it "Powerpoint horror" because there's moments where the phone glitches and it just sits there. You have to click to advance the glitchiness to increase how scary it is or something. I hate to just openly call out something for being bad design, but imagine you're on a roller coaster. The cart ratchets it's way to the top and you're about to go over the edge. Now you have to use a crank on the side of the roller coaster that lowers you down the drop a few steps at a time. Your stomach never drops, you don't get the adrenaline rush, your arm is getting tired from cranking the cart down though. I really wish this series would knock it off. The first game had loud phone call notifications that would make you jump, but sigh in relief, even a creepy unsettling moment here and there, but this one just tries to use super glitchy video effects. Which brings me to my next complaint. 

VFX
The game is at it's best when you're digging around the phone for answers and the dialogue options to guide people around. However, the absolute worst part is when it relies on fmv green screen vfx to tell a story. Look, I know. The budget doesn't really allow for Marvel movie level vfx, but there's a lot of green screen elements, really cheesy animations, and the acting isn't necessarily the best. I think a lot of the scenes could've been done inexpensively practically, but I'm guessing due to production issues, decisions were made to opt in for vfx instead. The "creepy" shadows and overly aggressive "glitchy" effects aren't really adding a lot to the game. 

The sound design is also particularly horrible in one section of the game. When the game is waiting for your response, the ambient sound levels are maxed out, but when you make a selection, the volume drops back down to normal. Not like a HUGE issue, but it's a glaringly obvious one I feel like should've been very easily caught. 

TLDR; 
The game isn't scary at all. It tries too hard and relies on cheesy vfx, cringey fmv (live action) moments, and puzzles that range from incredibly simple to very vague. Overall the story was just interesting enough for me to finish it, but nothing I'm going to talk about a few days from now.
